'''Carlo Miranda''' (15 August 1912 – 28 May 1982) was an Italian [[mathematician]], working on [[mathematical analysis]], [[Elliptic partial differential equation|theory of elliptic partial differential equations]] and [[complex analysis]]: he is known for giving the first proof of the [[Poincaré–Miranda theorem]],<ref>{{harv|Kulpa|1997|p=545}}.</ref> for [[Miranda's theorem]] in complex analysis,<ref>{{Harv|Burckel|1979|loc=p. 426, pp. 436–437, and pp. 456–457}}.</ref> and for writing an influential monograph in the theory of elliptic partial differential equations.<ref>See {{harv|Miranda|1955}} and its revised and translated second edition {{harv|Miranda|1970}}.</ref>
